chunks: And it was narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Aswad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Usamah al-Shahham, who said:

A man said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Should I delay the Maghrib prayer until the stars become visible?' He said, 'That is the way of the Khattabiyyah (followers of Khattab), for indeed Jibril (Gabriel) (peace be upon him) descended with it to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) at the time the sun's disk set.'
ai.seo_question: When should the Maghrib prayer be performed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precise onset of Maghrib prayer as the disappearance of the sun's disk, distinguishing it from the later time of 'stars appearing' which the Imam attributes to the Khattabiyyah sect. By linking this timing to Gabriel's revelation to the Prophet, the text underscores the divine origin of the prayer schedule and serves as a critical tool for distinguishing Shia jurisprudence from other sects regarding ritual timing.
